name: ScrollReveal-TS-TW
title: Scroll Reveal
description: Two paragraphs of copy sit on a black stage and come into focus progressively: each word rises from near-transparent and blurred to full clarity as it enters view, driven by scroll position.
use: Long-form copy or a manifesto section should pull the eye along as the reader scrolls.
avoid: Short pages or fast scrollers: the copy starts too faint to read until you scroll.
a11y: The copy is real text, but the scroll animation ignores reduced-motion and starts near-invisible. (keyboard: n-a, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Two short paragraphs of semibold type are stacked on black, the first white and the second muted grey, both left aligned with generous line spacing. No other elements are on screen.
behaves: As the block travels up the page every word climbs from faint and blurred to sharp and fully opaque, and the first paragraph straightens out of a slight tilt. Scrolling back reverses the whole sequence.
customise: The copy is passed as children; blur switch, base opacity, tilt angle, blur amount, end positions and class names are props. Word splitting is fixed.
weight: light: Scroll-triggered tweens on a handful of word spans; nothing heavy runs per frame.
